name: Mondscheinspitze
kurzbeschreibung: Viewpoint mountain (2,106 m) in the Karwendel with a stunning panoramic view over Achensee, the Karwendelgebirge, and as far as the Zillertaler Alpen.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Mondscheinspitze (2,106 m) reigns as a striking, symmetrical limestone pyramid in the Pre-Karwendel Range, poised dramatically between the Achen Valley and the Riß Valley. Situated west of Lake Achensee above the picturesque Gerntal valley, this elegant mountain is widely celebrated as one of the most rewarding panoramic summit destinations in the entire Karwendel Nature Park. Its poetic name ("Moonlight Peak") stems from centuries-old alpine lore describing how the summit rock glowed in silvery radiance beneath full moonlit skies, guiding local hunters and shepherds. Hikers who conquer the rigorous ascent are rewarded at the summit cross with an extraordinary 360-degree alpine panorama: gaze upon the turquoise expanse of Lake Achensee, the sheer cliffs of the Rofan mountains, the jagged ramparts of the Karwendel ranges, and the glaciated 3,000-meter giants of the Zillertal Alps.

Route & Requirements

The classic and most scenic route commences at the Gernalm alpine inn (1,172 m) at the head of the Gerntal valley near Pertisau. A well-graded farm lane winds up through subalpine forest and alpine meadows toward the Plumsjoch Pass and the rustic Plumsjochhütte (1,630 m). Here, the route turns north, tackling steep grassy slopes, rocky gullies, and limestone shoulders toward the ridge saddle. The final approach along the exposed western ridge demands absolute surefootedness and a calm head for heights on rugged alpine terrain (rated T3+/T4), with fixed steel cables aiding hikers across scrambly rock steps (UIAA grade I). Overcoming roughly 950 vertical meters over 9.5 kilometers, the round trip requires 5 to 6 hours of walking time. An alternative, even more demanding ascent begins in Achenkirch via the Schleimsattel. Rigid ankle-high mountain boots, trekking poles, layered weather protection, and plenty of water are vital, as there are no natural water sources along the rocky summit crest. Due to sharp limestone steps and wire-assisted drops, this tour is unsuitable for dogs.

Visit & Arrival

Public transit arrives via ÖBB mainline trains into Jenbach station, followed by regional VVT bus line 4080 to Pertisau at Lake Achensee. During the summer hiking season, a local valley shuttle connects Pertisau directly to the trailhead at Gernalm. Drivers take the Inntal autobahn A12 to exit Wiesing/Achensee, following federal highway B181 north toward Maurach and Pertisau. From Pertisau, a scenic 5-kilometer toll road leads through the Gerntal valley directly to the spacious hiker parking lot at the Gernalm inn.

Tips

Given the south-facing slopes, an early start around 6:00 or 7:00 AM is strongly advised in midsummer to beat both the heat and potential afternoon thunderstorms. After descending, treat yourself to fresh Tyrolean Kaiserschmarrn pancakes with plum compote on the sunny terrace of Plumsjochhütte or Gernalm. Bring compact binoculars to spot chamois grazing along the sheer scree gullies.
